measurement_diagnostic: The first sustained probe used a 1s poll-latency cutoff and produced no accepted steady window; streams and accounting passed. The slower original stats endpoint needs explicit HTTP-time uncertainty bounds. Its completed response is retained separately from the paired v2 steady corpus.
limitations: Single GPU with CPU offload; not NVLink or multi-GPU results.
Fixed output uses ignore_eos, temperature0 and Medium reasoning.
Latency workloads share shapes but use different timestamp nonces.
SSE chunks are not kernel token timestamps; steady rates use cumulative frontend counters.
Per-active-request steady rate is aggregate/C, not a per-user fairness guarantee.
Quality probes establish only the recorded tasks; weights and precision were unchanged.
262144 KV tokens are shared, not allocated independently to every session.
Four clients test a queue with at most three active requests.

selection_reason: Select prefill-first with three active requests and exact graph ceiling 3. Paired sustained medians are 42.29/49.54/58.27 aggregate tokens/s for C=1/2/3 against 41.85/49.63/42.59 on the original service. The C=3 gain is 36.8%; C=1/2 remain close to control. Completed short-output waves also improve. The selection follows the user's preference for sustained generation over earlier first output. Fair is retained as an opt-in alternative; the separately screened 500 ms/graph-4 variant reduces long arrival pauses but does not improve C=3 sustained throughput. These are limited synthetic workload measurements, not a guarantee for every context size or real coding project.
